::: {.callout-note}
**This is Joel Adams' lab, and his page has the instructions.** Do it in the
lab on **Tuesday Dec 8**. It follows Friday's and Monday's classes on
parallelism and OpenMP.
:::

## Objectives

Joel's page lists them: profiling, compile-time optimization, multicore CPUs,
threads, and OpenMP. You take a program that counts how often a short DNA
sequence (`CAT`) appears in the cat genome, about 2.5 billion characters, and
make it faster, first by improving the sequential code and then by running it
on several threads.

## The instructions

```{=html}
<p style="text-align:center;margin:1.2rem 0">
  <a class="btn btn-primary" href="https://cs.calvin.edu/courses/cs/112/adams/labs/genScan/"
```

Follow his page from the top. Part I makes the sequential program faster.
Part II runs it on several threads with OpenMP.

## Getting the Code {#getting-the-code}

Your private GitHub repository for this assignment is created for you inside
the course organization, with Joel's starting code already in it:
`genScan.cpp`, `OO_MPI_IO.h` and the `Makefile`. **Skip the step on his page
that downloads those three files.** You already have them.

```bash
gh repo clone 26fa-cs112/cs112-a15-YOURUSERNAME
cd cs112-a15-YOURUSERNAME
make
```

If `gh repo clone` cannot find your repository, see
[Getting the Code in a14](a14.qmd#getting-the-code): the same steps apply.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Do not put the genome in your repository folder.** It is about 2.5 GB. Keep
it in `/tmp`, as the lab says. GitHub refuses a file that large, and every push
after it would fail.
:::

## What to Submit

1. Your final `genScan.cpp` and `Makefile`.
2. The lab's spreadsheet, both tabs, each exported as a PDF and saved in your
   repository as `sequential.pdf` and `parallel.pdf`.

```bash
git add genScan.cpp Makefile sequential.pdf parallel.pdf
git commit -m "Complete a15"
git push
```

::: {.callout-important}
Put your name at the top of `README.md` before your final push.
:::

There is no `make test` for this one. It is graded on what you submit.
